extracted.intended_audience: AI researchers and practitioners evaluating or building large language models
extracted.subtask_short: evaluating LLM tool use and interactivity
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and evaluation dimensions for a language model's interactive behavior and use of external tools/APIs (e.g., search, calculators, email/calendar APIs, command line, simulated environments). Focuses on identification, invocation, orchestration, parsing of tool outputs, and embodied interaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactivity (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interactivity is the ability to communicate and respond to feedback from other agents, tools, and environments. It requires an agent to comprehend complex ideas, learn quickly, and learn from experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interactivity enables acquisition and application of knowledge, problem solving, adaptation, and achieving goals beyond the agent alone. The paper uses interactivity as a high-level dimension of intelligence and evaluates tool use and embodied interaction as two sub-dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tool use: access external resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Use external resources, such as search engines, calculators, or other APIs, to perform tasks that are difficult or impossible for the agent alone (e.g., overcome lack of current world knowledge, perform symbolic operations, execute code).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include SEARCH("query"), CALC(expression), CHARACTER(string,index). Evaluation checks whether the model calls appropriate tools to obtain current info or compute values instead of relying on outdated parametric knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify needed tools/functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to list which tools (or API functions) are needed in order to solve a task without demonstrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix example: GPT-4 lists four API functions needed to complete a task and then proceeds to use them effectively. Evaluation looks for explicit identification of required functions before execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct tool invocation / function calling
rubrics_metrics.description: When a tool is needed, the model should call it with the appropriate function name and correct arguments (e.g., issuing SEARCH("query"), CALC(expr)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures show the model calling SEARCH, CALC, CHARACTER, EMAIL.send, CALENDAR.add_event, etc. Incorrect invocation (wrong args, wrong semantics) is an error mode to track.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parsing and reasoning over tool outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: The model must correctly parse outputs returned by tools (search snippets, calculator results, file contents, command-line responses) and incorporate them into coherent answers or actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: SEARCH returns multiple - sometimes conflicting - snippets; GPT-4 can infer the correct answer despite conflicting snippets. Evaluation includes whether the model extracts relevant facts and reconciles contradictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tool orchestration / sequencing
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to use multiple tools in combination, in the correct order, to solve complex tasks (e.g., use search to find information, summarize pages, then CALC to compute values).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: managing calendar/email requires retrieving calendar events, sending/receiving emails, interpreting replies, and then adding an event. Success is measured by correct sequencing and integration of outputs across APIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal instruction / zero-shot tool generalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to use the tools with very minimal instruction and no demonstrations (zero-shot), generalizing to the provided API descriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper notes GPT-4 can use tools with minimal instruction and no specialized fine-tuning; evaluation checks whether the model needs demonstrations or adapts zero-shot from brief descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deciding when to call tools vs rely on internal knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason about whether to use an external tool or answer directly from parametric knowledge (e.g., do not call search for trivially known facts like the capital of France).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A limitation noted: GPT-4 sometimes uses a search engine for facts it could answer without one. Evaluation considers efficiency and appropriateness of tool usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness and error recovery from environment responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Detect failures or error messages from tools/environments and adapt commands or strategy to recover (e.g., correct wrong command syntax after seeing 'Could not find...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Zoo example: GPT-4 issued incorrect commands for filenames with spaces, observed the error, and corrected itself. Evaluation tracks ability to self-correct without human intervention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding fabrication / fidelity to external data
rubrics_metrics.description: When asked to read or act on external data/files, the model should use the actual content and avoid fabricating details (e.g., do not invent email replies or file contents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure case: GPT-4 fabricated content when replying to emails instead of reading files; this was fixed by prompt tweaks. Evaluators should look for hallucinations when dealing with external data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptation to unusual APIs / API semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Correctly adapt to nonstandard or unusual API function semantics rather than assuming standard behavior (e.g., reverse_get_character returns n'th-to-last char).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure 5.7: GPT-4 failed to use unusual tools initially, calling them as if they had standard semantics; evaluation should include tests with odd function definitions to check semantic adaptation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling free-form outputs and ambiguity in coordination tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpret free-form human or third-party responses (e.g., 'Tuesday or Wednesday Night', 'any day Monday-Thursday') and combine them with schedule constraints to make decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calendar/email example: GPT-4 combined ambiguous replies and calendar constraints to pick Wednesday. Evaluation looks for correct constraint reasoning and resolution of natural-language ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compositional command generation (command-line / scripting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generate sequences of correct command-line or API calls to complete multi-step tasks that manipulate files, rename items, relocate items, and produce explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Zoo manager example required >100 commands to complete six tasks. Evaluation checks whether the model can plan and execute many-step command sequences and produce required outputs (e.g., echo explanations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Embodied interaction: simulated environment comprehension
rubrics_metrics.description: Use natural language as a text interface to explore and manipulate simulated environments (maps, text-based games), understanding context, goals, actions, and outcomes and adapting over turns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warmup: navigating a map shows GPT-4 describing explored portions accurately. Text-based games require exploration, inventory manipulation, and valid command generation. Evaluation includes coverage of exploration and task completion in the environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit API specification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a task, the system should be provided or be able to propose the required API functions (names and argument structure) it will call to accomplish the task.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calendar/email example lists necessary functions (CALENDAR.add_event, EMAIL.send, etc.). Evaluation may include whether the model requests or defines suitable API interfaces for the requested operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overcoming standard LLM weaknesses via tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Use tools to mitigate known LLM weaknesses (lack of current world knowledge, weak symbolic manipulation, inability to execute code).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: SEARCH for up-to-date facts (current president), CALC for precise arithmetic, executing commands for file operations. Success is judged by whether external tools effectively compensate for parametric weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure of task success / completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Success metrics include whether the model completes the requested multi-step tasks, produces correct final outputs, and uses tools appropriately to reach a correct solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper reports qualitative success (e.g., 'was able to solve almost all tasks') and notes specific failures; formal evaluation should record completion, correctness, and types of errors (fabrication, wrong arguments, repetition of error patterns).
